title: Writing a scalar into the in-memory handle backed by that same scalar moves from the buffer SvGROW has freed
live_proof: upstream fixed it in 254b30e378 (254b30e378233c89ec38c20974da4ff71b6f9821) (2026-02-14). That commit is an ancestor of v5.45.3-85-gdb19522155 and is NOT an ancestor of the v5.36.3 tag (checked with git merge-base --is-ancestor, both directions), so it never reached the 5.36 maintenance branch; the pin's tree shows the unfixed code (pin ext/PerlIO-scalar/scalar.xs:261 Move(vbuf, dst + offset, count, char) after the SvGROW at scalar.xs:229/253). Host ASan at the pin: ASan: heap-use-after-free (rc=77); the same trigger, same harness and same ASan options on master: no report (rc=0, the harness reports [PASS])
fidelity: the trigger is the test upstream added with its own fix, extracted onto a self-contained harness that collects failures instead of aborting, so one script yields one verdict. It is upstream's own reproduction, not a reduction of ours; what it does NOT establish is which arm ought to catch it

sysalloc-none.oracle: no fault: completes, the workload's own oracle fails

sysalloc-bounds.oracle: no fault: completes, the workload's own oracle fails

sysalloc-sublet.oracle: no fault: completes, the workload's own oracle fails

sublet-svheads.oracle: no fault: completes, the workload's own oracle fails

cheribsd-revocation.oracle: SIGPROT: the defence reports; with revocation off (_RUNTIME_REVOCATION_DISABLE=1) the same binary gives: no report: completes

status: all four Capstone arms measured 2026-10-06 on the Capstone application VM, each after passing its own two controls; cheribsd-revocation measured 2026-10-06 on CheriBSD purecap, revocation selected per process because the system-wide default kills the guest's sshd, and every case run under both settings so the pair controls the knob (results/20261006-cheribsd)
harness_limit: applies to the four CAPSTONE arms only. The defect does not execute in a Capstone domain: a probe on the bounds arm shows the in-memory filehandle this case needs accepts its writes and discards them -- open returns 1, print returns 1, and the backing scalar is still undef afterwards, where the host build has the full 52-byte string -- so the overlapping Move that IS the defect is never reached and this case is outside those four arms' denominator. cheribsd-revocation runs a complete FreeBSD Perl, where the layer works: the defect executes and revocation CATCHES it (SIGPROT with revocation on, clean with it off). So the case is live and catchable, and what the Capstone arms show here is a gap in the domain's PerlIO, not in the heap
